links.outcome: Errors from IOL models not in AI training due to delayed updates
links.effect: 7.3% of 9713 post-implementation IOL surgeries involved unlearned lenses, leading to two incorrect IOL implantations; model updated only three times due to budget and stability constraints.
links.quote: Of the 9713 IOL surgeries performed post implementation, 7.3% involved unlearned lenses, leading to two cases of incorrect IOL implantation.

links.outcome: Surgical safety failures despite accurate AI detection in the clinical workflow
links.effect: Pre-implementation testing demonstrated 100% accuracy in 300 cases; deployment included a wrong-eye anaesthetic injection despite AI warnings, which the nurse could not relay even after eight attempts.
links.quote: The AI-based surgery safety system continued to point out the mistake, but the attending nurse could not relay this to the surgeon even after eight attempts, leading to a local anaesthetic injection in the wrong eye.

links.outcome: Medical errors when AI authentication was not implemented or properly used
links.effect: Five postimplementation errors (0.027%) occurred, four in non-authenticated cases. Initial surgical laterality authentication was 84.5% vs 99.4% post implementation; two laterality errors occurred during initial implementation.
links.quote: Post implementation, five medical errors (0.027%) occurred, with four in non-authenticated cases (where the AI system was not fully implemented or properly used), compared with one (0.0053%) pre-implementation (p=0.125).

unlisted_practices: Add AI-based patient identification, surgical laterality verification, and intraocular lens authentication to the existing WHO Surgical Safety Checklist.

links.effect: 30 near misses (0.16%) were identified post-implementation versus 9 (0.048%) pre-implementation.
links.quote: The AI system identified 30 near misses (0.16%) post implementation, vs 9 (0.048%) pre-implementation (p=0.00067), surgical laterality errors/near misses occurred at 0.039% (7/18 762) and IOL recognition at 0.29% (28/9713).

links.effect: Potential benefits ranged from US$181,946.94 to US$2,769,129.12 in conservative and intermediate scenarios.
links.quote: Cost-benefit analysis revealed potential benefits ranging from US$181 946.94 to US$2 769 129.12 in conservative and intermediate scenarios, respectively.

links.effect: Four of five post-implementation medical errors occurred in non-authenticated cases where the AI was not properly used.
links.quote: Post implementation, five medical errors (0.027%) occurred, with four in non-authenticated cases (where the AI system was not fully implemented or properly used), compared with one (0.0053%) pre-implementation (p=0.125).

links.effect: Two errors involved unlearned intraocular lenses due to delayed AI updates, causing non-authentication.
links.quote: Of the four non-authenticated errors, two were laterality errors during the initial implementation period and two were IOL implantation errors involving unlearned IOLs (7.3% of cases) due to delayed AI updates.

links.effect: The system demonstrated 100% accuracy in a pre-implementation test of 300 cases.
links.quote: Pre-implementation testing with 300 cases (50% intentionally erroneous) demonstrated 100% system accuracy ( online supplemental figure 6 ).

unlisted_practices: Integrating AI-based surgical safety checks with the existing WHO Surgical Safety Checklist

screen.reason: Evaluates the real-world implementation of an AI-based surgical safety checklist verification system (patient ID, laterality, and IOL check) before and after deployment across over 37,000 ophthalmic surgeries.
